main_body: Thatched-roof hut: a large stepped thatch roof slope (rows 0-37) over a timber front wall with a plank door, a shuttered window and a stone doorstep (rows 38-63)
top_band: The thatch roof slope is the top surface. It runs from the ridge at row 0 down to a lighter eave band at rows ~34-35 (#f0d888/#dcb85a), with scalloped thatch courses in several tones. Below it is a dark eave shadow at rows 36-38, then the wall.
evidence: The roof is a big foreshortened slope with lit thatch courses and a distinct light eave edge. A dark overhang shadow sits under the eave, then a separate vertical wall face with its own shading. The door has a dark inset frame and lintel shadow, and the window has an inset dark opening with a sill. This is the same structure as the reference houses (roof slope over wall), with no receding side face. The roof reads as the top surface and the wall as the south face.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 6 lightness steps (L 70, 96, 126, 156, 184, 214) in scalloped courses with per-clump highlights. The wall planks carry vertical grain, and the door has dark iron bands and a handle. Outlines are a dark brown tinted to the adjacent material (0% neutral edge pixels), not a black sticker line. Flat-fill coverage is 0%. Density is lower than the references (8 colours per tile vs 11 and 18, and 29 distinct colours vs 66 and 185), but the piece is small and its palette is a locked single-hue one. The surfaces are still shaded and textured, so it would sit acceptably next to the references.
